translations.literal: Guizhou
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou

sentences.zh: 貴州：禹貢荊、梁二州徼外之域。

translations.literal: Guizhou: a region beyond the marches of the Jing and Liang domains in the Tribute of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Guizhou lay outside the frontiers of the Jing and Liang regions described in the Tribute of Yu.

sentences.zh: 清初沿明制，設貴州布政使司，為貴州省。

translations.literal: In the early Qing, following Ming institutions, the Guizhou Provincial Administration Commission was established, making Guizhou a province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qing, the dynasty retained Ming arrangements, established the Guizhou Provincial Administration Commission, and constituted Guizhou as a province.

sentences.zh: 順治十六年，設巡撫，治貴陽，並設雲貴總督，分駐兩省。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Shunzhi, a provincial governor was established, with seat at Guiyang, and the Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General was also established, with separate residences in the two provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 16 (1659), a provincial governor was appointed with his seat at Guiyang, and a Yunnan-Guizhou governor-general was created, each province receiving its own headquarters.

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi, the title was changed to Governor of Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 (1662), the post was retitled Governor of Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，仍為雲貴總督，駐貴州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, it was again made the Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General, stationed at Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 4 (1665), the office reverted to Yunnan-Guizhou Governor-General, headquartered at Guizhou.

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, the headquarters were moved to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 21 (1682), the headquarters were transferred to Yunnan.

translations.literal: Formerly it administered ten prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: It originally governed ten prefectures.

sentences.zh: 康熙三年，增置黔西、平遠、大定、威寧四府。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kangxi, four prefectures were added: Qianxi, Pingyuan, Dading, and Weining.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 3 (1664), four prefectures were added—Qianxi, Pingyuan, Dading, and Weining.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，大定、平遠、黔西降州，隸威寧府。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Dading, Pingyuan, and Qianxi were reduced to subprefectures and placed under Weining Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 22 (1683), Dading, Pingyuan, and Qianxi were demoted to subprefectures subordinate to Weining Prefecture.

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yongzheng, Nanlong Prefecture was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 5 (1727), Nanlong Prefecture was established.

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Zunyi was detached from Sichuan and placed under this province.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 6 (1728), Zunyi was transferred from Sichuan and annexed to Guizhou.

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Dading was again promoted and Weining was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 7 (1729), Dading was restored to prefectural rank and Weining was demoted.

sentences.zh: 乾隆四十一年，升仁懷，嘉慶二年，升松桃，均為直隸廳，改南籠為興義府。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Qianlong, Renhuai was promoted; in the second year of Jiaqing, Songtao was promoted—both to directly administered departments; Nanlong was changed to Xingyi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 41 (1776), Renhuai was elevated; in Jiaqing 2 (1797), Songtao was elevated—each becoming a directly administered department—and Nanlong was renamed Xingyi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三年，降平越府為直隸州。

translations.literal: In the third year, Pingyue Prefecture was reduced to a directly administered subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 3 (1798), Pingyue Prefecture was demoted to a directly administered subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 十四年，升普安為直隸州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Pu'an was promoted to a directly administered subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 14 (1809), Pu'an was raised to a directly administered subprefecture.

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, it was changed to a department.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing 16 (1811), it was converted to a department.

translations.idiomatic: North polar altitude ranged from 25°04′ to 28°33′.

translations.idiomatic: Longitude west of the capital ranged from 7°33′ to 10°55′.

sentences.zh: 宣統三年，編戶一百七十七萬一千五百三十三，口八百五十萬三千九百五十四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuantong, registered households numbered one million seven hundred seventy-one thousand five hundred thirty-three; population eight million five hundred three thousand nine hundred fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 3 (1911), registered households totaled 1,771,533 and population 8,503,954.

sentences.zh: 共領府十二，直隸廳三，直隸州一，廳十一，州十三，縣三十四，土司五十三。

translations.literal: In all it administered twelve prefectures, three directly administered departments, one directly administered subprefecture, eleven departments, thirteen subprefectures, thirty-four counties, and fifty-three native chieftaincies.
translations.idiomatic: In all it governed twelve prefectures, three directly administered departments, one directly administered subprefecture, eleven departments, thirteen subprefectures, thirty-four counties, and fifty-three native chieftain domains.

translations.idiomatic: Courier routes: one ran east from Zhenxiong Pass to Huangzhou in Hunan;

translations.literal: one westward crossing Guansuo Ridge reaching Pingyi in Yunnan;
translations.idiomatic: one west over Guansuo Ridge to Pingyi in Yunnan;

translations.literal: one northwest crossing the Liuguang River reaching Yongning in Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: one northwest across the Liuguang River to Yongning in Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 電線：北通重慶、畢節，又分達威寧至雲南。

translations.literal: Telegraph lines: north to Chongqing and Bijie, with branches from Weining to Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Telegraph lines ran north to Chongqing and Bijie, with a branch from Weining into Yunnan.

translations.literal: Guiyang Prefecture: key, busy, difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Guiyang Prefecture: rated key, busy, and difficult.

sentences.zh: 巡撫、布政使、提學使、按察使、糧儲道同駐。

translations.literal: The provincial governor, provincial administration commissioner, education intendant, judicial commissioner, and grain intendant were all stationed here.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial governor, administration commissioner, education intendant, judicial commissioner, and grain intendant all had their seats here.

sentences.zh: 光緒三十四年裁糧儲道，設巡警道、勸業道。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year of Guangxu the grain intendant was abolished; police and industry intendancies were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 34 (1908), the grain intendant was abolished and police and industry intendancies were created.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年改按察使為提法使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong the judicial commissioner was changed to procuratorial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuantong 1 (1909), the judicial commissioner was retitled procuratorial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 順治初，因明為軍民府，領州三，縣一。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shunzhi, following the Ming, it was a military-civilian prefecture administering three subprefectures and one county.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shunzhi, following Ming practice, it was a military-civilian prefecture governing three subprefectures and one county.

sentences.zh: 康熙十一年，增置龍里縣。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Kangxi, Longli County was added.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 11 (1672), Longli County was established.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，裁「軍民」字，增置貴築、修文二縣，又改平越府之貴定來隸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year, the words "military-civilian" were dropped; Guizhu and Xiuwen counties were added, and Guiding of Pingyue Prefecture was transferred here.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 (1687), the "military-civilian" designation was removed; Guizhu and Xiuwen counties were added; and Guiding was transferred from Pingyue Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 三十四年，省新貴入貴築。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, Xingui was merged into Guizhu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 34 (1695), Xingui was annexed to Guizhu.

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongzheng, Changzhai Department was established.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 4 (1726), Changzhai Department was established.

sentences.zh: 光緒七年，以羅斛州判地置廳，移長寨同知駐，降長寨為鎮，併入定番。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Guangxu, a department was established on the territory of the Luohu subprefectural magistrate; the Changzhai subprefect was moved there; Changzhai was reduced to a town and merged into Dingfan.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu 7 (1881), a department was created from Luohu subprefectural territory; the Changzhai subprefect was relocated there; Changzhai was demoted to a town and merged into Dingfan.

translations.idiomatic: The Jigong River enters from northern Qingzhen and exits north again into Qingzhen.

sentences.zh: 貫城河出崆巃山，合城北擇溪水入城中，南流注南明河。

translations.idiomatic: The Guancheng River rises on Konglong Mountain, picks up the Zexi north of the city, runs through the walls, and flows south into the Nanming.
